seo.description: How long does Percocet stay in your system? Learn urine, blood, saliva, and hair detection times, plus what affects them and where to find help.

hero.headline: How Long Does Percocet Stay in Your System?

sections.heading: TL;DR
body: How long does Percocet stay in your system? In most people, it clears the blood within about 24 hours, but oxycodone stays detectable in urine for 1–4 days, in saliva for 1–2 days, and in hair for up to 90 days. Below, you will learn how Percocet is metabolized, what affects those timelines, and when detection may signal a deeper problem worth addressing.

If you are asking how long does Percocet stay in your system, you may be facing a drug test, managing a prescription, or quietly worrying that use has gotten out of hand. Whatever brought you here, the honest answer is: it depends. Because several personal factors shape the timeline, detection windows are ranges rather than fixed numbers. Still, understanding the basics can help you make informed, safer decisions.

sections.heading: What Is Percocet?
body: Percocet is a prescription painkiller that combines two ingredients: oxycodone, a powerful opioid, and acetaminophen, the pain reliever found in Tylenol [1]. Doctors prescribe it for moderate to severe pain, often after surgery or injury. Because oxycodone is a Schedule II opioid, however, it carries a significant risk of dependence and addiction. That risk is exactly why detection timelines matter to so many people.

sections.heading: How Long Does Percocet Stay in Your System?
body: So, how long does Percocet stay in your system overall? The pain-relieving effects typically last 4 to 6 hours, yet the drug lingers far longer than the relief does [1]. Oxycodone has a half-life of roughly 3 to 4 hours, which means your body eliminates about half of a dose in that time. As a result, it usually takes around 19 to 24 hours to clear most of the drug from your bloodstream. Even then, metabolites remain detectable in other tissues.

sections.heading: Percocet Detection Times by Test Type
body: The answer to how long does Percocet stay in your system changes depending on the test used. Urine screening is the most common method, while hair testing offers the longest look back [2]. The table below summarizes typical windows.

sections.heading: What Affects How Long Percocet Stays in Your System?
body: No two bodies process opioids identically. Consequently, the same dose can clear at very different rates from one person to the next. Several factors influence the timeline.
Age, since metabolism tends to slow over time
Liver and kidney function, which drive elimination
Dose and how long you have been taking it
Body composition and hydration
Other medications that interact with oxycodone
Because of these variables, published detection windows are estimates. Heavy or long-term use, for example, can extend them.

sections.heading: How Percocet Is Metabolized
body: Once swallowed, oxycodone reaches peak blood levels within 1 to 2 hours [1]. From there, the liver breaks it down into metabolites such as noroxycodone. Afterward, the kidneys filter these compounds out through urine. Meanwhile, the acetaminophen component is processed separately, which is why exceeding the dose can strain the liver. This dual makeup makes careful dosing especially important.

sections.heading: Signs Percocet Use May Be a Problem
body: Sometimes the question behind the question is not really about a test. If you find yourself anxious about results, that concern itself can be telling [3]. Warning signs of opioid dependence include the following.
Needing more to feel the same effect (tolerance)
Taking Percocet longer or more often than prescribed
Experiencing withdrawal when a dose is missed
Unsuccessful attempts to cut back
Continuing use despite negative consequences

sections.heading: Percocet Withdrawal and Why Detox Matters
body: Never stop Percocet abruptly after regular use. Doing so can trigger uncomfortable opioid withdrawal, including muscle aches, nausea, chills, and cravings [2]. Although withdrawal is rarely life-threatening on its own, medical supervision makes it far safer and more manageable. Therefore, a supervised detox is strongly recommended over quitting cold turkey. From there, therapy can address the roots of dependence.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
body: 1. How long does Percocet stay in your system for a urine test?Oxycodone is typically detectable in urine for 1 to 4 days after the last dose, though heavy or long-term use can extend that window.
2. Can Percocet show up on a hair test?Yes. Hair testing has the longest detection window, showing oxycodone use for up to 90 days, which makes it useful for identifying chronic use.

3. How long does it take for Percocet to leave your bloodstream?Most of the drug clears the blood within about 24 hours, since oxycodone’s half-life is roughly 3 to 4 hours. Metabolites may linger longer in other tissues.
4. Does drinking water flush Percocet out faster?Staying hydrated supports normal kidney function, but it will not meaningfully speed elimination or reliably alter a drug test result.
5. Will Percocet cause a positive opioid drug test?Yes. Oxycodone can trigger a positive on broad opioid screens. If you have a valid prescription, tell the testing site before your test.
